what_it_does: Processing long documents with a language model is slow because the attention step — where every word looks at every other word — scales quadratically: double the text length and the work quadruples. SampleAttention cuts that cost by skipping most of the attention computation, keeping only the small fraction of word-pairs that actually matter, while preserving accuracy above 99% of the full-computation baseline. It reduces the time-to-first-token by up to 5.29x on sequences of one million tokens.
method_in_detail:
The idea. When a language model computes attention, it calculates a score between every query word and every key word, producing a huge matrix of scores. In long documents, roughly 90% of these scores are so small that exponentiating them (to convert them to probabilities via the softmax step — the normalization that makes all scores sum to 1) makes them essentially zero. The trick is to find and compute only the important scores without first computing all of them.

The accuracy guide. SampleAttention introduces a metric called Cumulative Residual Attention (CRA): the minimum fraction of total attention probability that is retained after you mask away the low-importance entries. If CRA is 0.95, you kept 95% of the attention mass. Experiments show CRA correlates tightly with model accuracy, so setting a CRA threshold lets you trade off speed for quality in a principled way.

Stage 1 — chunked sampling. Instead of computing attention for all query words, the query sequence is divided into equal chunks. Only a small block of queries at the tail of each chunk is fully computed. These sample scores are then averaged (reduced) at a block granularity of 128 tokens in two directions: column (global tokens that many queries attend to) and slash (diagonal bands representing nearby context). This gives a cheap but accurate estimate of which blocks of key-value pairs matter.

Stage 2 — block filtering. Using the sampled scores, SampleAttention independently selects the fewest column-strip blocks and slash-strip blocks needed to meet the CRA threshold in each direction. It does this with a cumulative-sum top-k: sort the block scores, accumulate until you reach the threshold, and take those blocks. The selected indices are extended to cover the full sequence, merged into a single sparse mask, and used to run a sparse version of FlashAttention2 (a standard fast attention algorithm).

The key design choice. Decomposing the joint column+slash selection into two independent problems reduces the search from N² combinations to N+N, making the selection fast enough to run at inference time without pre-profiling per attention head.

The result. On ChatGLM4-9B, Yi-9B, and InternLM2-7B tested across RULER, LongBench, and InfiniteBench benchmarks, SampleAttention consistently scores above 99% of full-attention accuracy while achieving 1.15x–5.29x speedup over FlashAttention2 as sequence length grows from 32k to 1M tokens.
